transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood Support), Arjun Patel (Sentinel ML), Sara Gomez (Sentinel Eng), Noah Li (Sentinel ML Eng)

Summary: quick triage of a reported accuracy drop after quantizing production model to AWQ/INT8. Goal: decide immediate mitigations, reproduce locally/on-prem, and plan bisect and deployment path (hosted fallback, dedicated with pinning, or private on-prem).

Topics: quantization tradeoffs (GPTQ vs AWQ vs INT8 vs FP8), KV cache interactions, batching and latency impacts, on-prem/VPC restrictions, regression bisect plans, evaluation dataset and metric drift.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Lena: okay hi everyone, thanks for hopping on. I think we have about an hour. Arjun, wanna kick off with the symptom?
[00:12] Arjun: yeah, thanks. we started seeing a ~4 to 6 percent drop in answer-accuracy on our triage eval after we moved the 13B to AWQ INT variant in prod last week. it's not catastrophic but it's outside our SLO and customers are noticing subtle hallucinations.
[00:29] Sara: just to add, the latency improved by ~30% so there's a clear perf win, but tradeoff looks worse than we expected for our extractive QA flows.
[00:40] Diego: when you say AWQ INT variant, you mean the config Redwood suggested — block 8, group size 128, per-channel scale?
[00:49] Noah: yeah that's the one. we used the package from the private repo, applied the pruning script and then AWQ post-process.
[00:57] Lena: ok, good. first hypothesis: either AWQ quantization is causing layerwise outliers or kv-cache interaction is amplifying token-level errors under caching. second hypothesis: eval harness mismatch — different sampling seed/temperature between local benchmark and prod.
[01:14] Arjun: we did use temperature 0.0 for deterministic outputs. seed was not explicitly set in our serving infra, but we thought zero temp would be stable.
[01:23] Diego: note: Grep-uh — (laughs) sorry — I mean, the runtime's det-seed path for cached queries sometimes reuses non-deterministic kernels on older CUDA driver versions. we've seen that bite in the past. Could be a subtle source of non-determinism.
[01:37] Maya: also on KV, if prefix caching is enabled with mixed precision, the tensor cast can introduce rounding differences when recomputing KV segments during long-context streaming.
[01:48] Sara: how big is the eval set? maybe it's noise?
[01:51] Arjun: ~12k prompts, but the failing subset is around ~120 that flip labels consistently after quantize. we'll send those.
[01:58] Diego: perfect. Plan from our side: reproduce exactly, then run a per-layer bisect using 1) GPTQ baseline, 2) AWQ, 3) INT8 symmetric, 4) FP8 hybrid if you can allow it — FP8 needs a supported runtime build. we want per-layer activations and logits diffs.
[02:14] Lena: note schedule constraints if we do on-prem runs: the private environment has no egress so we'll need the model tar + instrumented runtime shipped and run by your infra, or Redwood's offline runner image.
[02:26] Sara: we prefer to run it ourselves on-prem for security reasons. what's involved in the runner image?
[02:31] Maya: it's a small docker image with an inference harness, the bisect script, and a lightweight profiler. it expects the model in a specific fs layout and a KMS endpoint for key unwrap if using encrypted artifacts. We can provide the runbook.
[02:43] Noah: KMS concerns — we use cloud KMS and can't export keys, so we need support for in-vpc KMS decrypt and local disk key cache for the run.
[02:51] Diego: yes, the on-prem flow supports a customer KMS agent and ephemeral keys. there's a step to bind the image to your VPC IPs. we'll include that in runbook.
[02:59] Arjun: back to the quantization: have you seen AWQ produce larger per-layer delta in the final FFN layers vs GPTQ? that was our initial observation.
[03:07] Diego: AWQ tends to bias small-magnitude weights differently because of asymmetric quant ranges. GPTQ's per-row retrain tends to preserve some rare high-frequency patterns better — but at cost of slower quant time and sometimes worse perf. AWQ is faster and smaller.
[03:22] Lena: to be explicit: we will run layered bisect to identify first layer where logits diverge beyond epsilon. We will also test inference with and without KV cache, and with batching disabled to check whether batching interactions hide the issue.
[03:36] Sara: will batching cause different numerical order or associativity that could explain diffs?
[03:40] Diego: absolutely. larger batch sums on FP16/FP32 ops can change rounding. When combined with quantized matmuls, accumulation path changes can flip some token predictions.
[03:49] Noah: regarding FP8: is it production-ready on Redwood runtime? we saw notes about experimental kernel support.
[03:55] Maya: FP8 is available behind a runtime flag and requires the newer nvptx kernels and cuDNN version — so on-prem you'll need that driver. In hosted we can flip it in a canary. FP8 sometimes recovers numeric fidelity vs aggressive INT8 depending on layer distribution.
[04:09] Arjun: what's the recommended fallback for prod while bisect is ongoing? roll back to GPTQ? or use hosted until we have a fix?
[04:17] Lena: options: 1) immediate rollback to GPTQ/FP16 variant for affected routes; 2) enable model routing: keep AWQ for low-latency non-critical flows and route QA-sensitive traffic to GPTQ; 3) restrict AWQ to shorter contexts where KV-cache not used. We'll provide cost delta estimates.
[04:33] Sara: option 2 seems interesting if routing is low effort. how hard is that to implement?
[04:37] Diego: in Redwood config it's a per-route routing policy — you can add a rule based on endpoint or request header. We can demo a canary policy.
[04:44] Arjun: for the bisect, what artifacts do you need from us?
[04:47] Diego: failing prompt list, the exact inference config (temp, top_p, seed if any), runtime docker image details including CUDA driver, and a few raw model checkpoints: the FP16 checkpoint we quantized from and the AWQ quantized artifact.
[04:58] Arjun: we'll send those tonight.
[05:01] Lena: good. Technical detail: we'll run per-layer activation diffs and also KL divergence of logits, and if we find issues at FFN or attention output, we'll attempt local re-quant with per-channel scaling and compare.
[05:13] Sara: can the runtime do per-layer mixed precision (e.g., keep last attention in FP16 while quantizing others)?
[05:19] Diego: yes, our runtime supports per-layer precision overrides and warm-starting a quantized model with selective FP16 kept. That's a common mitigant.
[05:27] Noah: how about KV cache invalidation — do we recompute cached keys after quantize or does caching layer re-interpret tensors?
[05:33] Maya: caching stores raw projected keys in the runtime's tensor format. If quantization changes projection weights, the previously cached keys are invalid. In long-lived streaming sessions you either need to flush cache at deploy or provide a migration path that replays context.
[05:47] Arjun: we saw flips mostly in long context (>1024 tokens) streaming scenarios, so that aligns with cache invalidation being a factor.
[05:54] Diego: another test: run identical prompt with cache disabled for both pre/post quantize; if diffs vanish, it's likely cache state mismatch or accumulation rounding across streaming updates.
[06:02] Lena: timeline: Diego runs bisect pipelines starting tomorrow; Maya packages the runner and runbook for your infra; Arjun will supply the failing prompt subset + artifacts; we'll reconvene once bisect surface is identified.
[06:12] Sara: any quick tunables we can try without rollback? maybe slight temp increase or top_p tweak?
[06:18] Diego: sometimes increasing temperature from 0 to 0.01 doesn't change top-1 deterministic tasks much, but for exact-match QA it can introduce more noise. I'd avoid that for now. Instead try per-route precision overrides — keep last two transformer blocks at FP16. That often fixes accuracy with modest perf hit.
[06:33] Noah: curious about AWQ's group size — we used group 128. is smaller group better for preserving accuracy?
[06:38] Diego: smaller group (64 or 32) reduces quantization granularity and can improve accuracy but increases size and slightly increases compute cost. We'll include expected perf tradeoffs in the bisect report.
[06:48] Arjun: driver versions — we're on NVIDIA driver 535. Do you have a specific minimum?
[06:52] Maya: for FP8 and the newer fused kernels we test on 545+, but AWQ/INT8 paths should be fine on 535. We'll still capture behavior differences across drivers.
[06:59] Lena: ok let's talk about audit and security asks. Arjun, you mentioned policy about no external artifacts in VPC. That means Redwood can't run hosted experiments for the encrypted models. We'll provide the signed runner image + instructions.
[07:12] Arjun: correct. we need the security slides.
[07:15] Lena: we'll send the security deck and the SRE contact.
[07:18] Diego: a quick note about instrumentation: add a logging flag to capture per-request kernel choice and quantization code path; that will help us correlate driver/kernel changes to regressions.
[07:28] Noah: good idea. We'll enable that for a subset of traffic.
[07:31] Sara: any other suggestions?
[07:33] Diego: one more: run logits vs reference and collect confusion clusters. If errors concentrate on small token sets, targeted post-quantize corrections (like bias correction on output layer) can fix most cases.
[07:44] Arjun: that could be lower friction than full rollback.
[07:46] Lena: final recap: Redwood runs bisect across quant variants, customer provides artifacts and will run on-prem bisect using runner, teams will evaluate per-layer diffs and consider per-layer FP16 keep or output bias-correction as mitigations. Next sync: tentative 2025-09-23 for results review.
[07:59] Sara: thanks everyone.
[08:01] Lena: thanks, end call.

Optional auto-summaries: 
- Root cause candidates: per-layer quantization deltas (AWQ asymmetric ranges), KV-cache mismatch for long-context streaming, driver/kernel non-determinism, and batching numerical associativity differences.
- Short-term mitigations: route QA-sensitive traffic to GPTQ/FP16; keep final transformer blocks in FP16; flush KV cache on deploy for streaming endpoints.
- Long-term: add per-layer mixed precision profiles to deployment pipeline, expand nightly regression harness to include streaming/long-context tests, and auto-bisect tooling for quantized artifacts.

References to shared artifacts:
- Benchmarks sheet (link above) — raw per-prompt diffs and perf numbers will be uploaded.
- Security deck for on-prem/VPC runner (link above).

End of transcript.
